title: Adjunction combination of the three comparison squares
statement: Let C,C₀,E,E₀ be monoidal categories, Q:C→E and Q₀:C₀→E₀ lax monoidal functors, F⊣T and D⊣R adjunctions, a:Q₀⋙D→F⋙Q and b:T⋙Q₀→Q⋙R natural transformations. Suppose δ:D(A⊗B)≅DA⊗DB is natural, t:F(A⊗B)→FA⊗FB satisfies the tensor square with a, and D(bK);ε(QK)=a(TK);Q(εK). For K,L,I and m:TK⊗TL→T(K⊗L), assume F(m);ε(K⊗L)=t(TK,TL);(εK⊗εL). For every φ:K⊗L→I, (bK⊗bL);transpose(δ;ε⊗ε);R(μQ;Qφ)=μQ₀;Q₀(m;Tφ);bI. This purely categorical result uses only the stated equations.

source.place: Lemma 20.31.3, the adjunction polygon proof; assumed tensor and counit squares are Tags 0FP0/0FP1

proof.text: Apply injectivity of the inverse adjunction Hom equivalence. Its left and right naturality compute the two transposes. Naturality of δ and the counit square replace the two derived counits; lax tensor naturality and the tensor square move to Q of the ordinary evaluation. Use the ordinary evaluation identity and naturality of a to identify the paths. Postcompose by R(Qφ) and use naturality of b.
